# papertooth 0.5.2 — complete documentation

> Hand-drawn Japanese stationery for the web: dotted paper, highlighters, ink, pencil, hanko stamps, washi tape and planner pieces, in CSS with an optional script.

MIT · © Plain Matter Pte Ltd · https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/



---

# Introduction

Hand-drawn stationery for the web. Paper-makers call the fine grain on a sheet its tooth: it is what grips the pencil and what you feel under your fingers. Papertooth brings that feel to a web page, inspired by Japanese stationery.

Writing that looks like it was done by hand, on paper you can almost feel.
Text sits on the dots. Links get a [pen underline](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/link/), a phrase can be picked out with a highlighter, and a word can be circled in red pencil.

[Get started](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/install/)[Browse the kit](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/highlighter/)

Every element has a playground

済 Approved

## What is inside

[**Paper and writing** Paper, ruling, typed and handwritten text](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/paper/)[**Marks** Highlighters, underlines, separators, marks, stamps](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/highlighter/)[**Paper goods** Sticky notes, tape, cards, clips, labels](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/sticky/)[**Images** Lithograph, printer, frames](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/litho/)[**Planner** Day, week, habits, bullet journal](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/planner/)[**Forms** Checkboxes, radios, text fields](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/checkbox/)[**Diagrams** Flowcharts, pie and bar charts from Mermaid](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/flowchart/)

## How it works

The CSS works on its own: paper, tape, notes, stamps, forms and every variant are classes and data attributes. A small optional script adds what CSS cannot do: ink textures as SVG filters, shapes drawn at each element's real size, text snapped to the grid, image effects and diagrams. It draws only what is near the screen and goes fully idle afterwards.

Nothing is rotated unless you ask for it. Give any note, stamp, tape, card or photo a `--pt-rot` to set it at an angle.

Anything drawn can be drawn with any instrument: fountain pen, ballpoint, brush pen, felt marker, graphite or coloured pencil. Put `data-tool` on it.

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Installation

*papertooth · Getting started*

Install the package, or load two files from a CDN.

npm

```
npm install papertooth
```

```
import 'papertooth/css';
import { init } from 'papertooth';

const kit = init({ pen: 'ink-ai', motion: 'scroll' });
```

CDN, no build step

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/papertooth@0.5/dist/papertooth.min.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/papertooth@0.5/dist/papertooth.min.js" defer data-pt-auto></script>
```

`data-pt-auto` starts the script on load. Pass options as JSON: `data-pt-auto='{"seed": 7}'`. The running instance is `window.Papertooth.kit`.

## Fonts

Fonts are not bundled. The defaults are Courier Prime, Special Elite and Caveat, plus Shippori Mincho B1 and Zen Maru Gothic for Japanese stamps. Swap any of them in [Theming](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/theming/).

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Caveat:wght@400;700&family=Courier+Prime:wght@400;700&family=Special+Elite&display=swap">
```

## A first page

```
<body class="pt-desk">
  <main class="pt-sheet" data-paper="dot">
    <h1 class="pt-wobble">A typed heading</h1>
    <p>Some text with a <mark class="pt-mark">highlight</mark> and a <a class="pt-link" href="#">link</a>.</p>
    <a class="pt-btn" href="#">Hire me</a>
  </main>
</body>
```

## Without the script

Everything still renders, with a fixed version of each drawn shape. For the textures, paste `dist/papertooth-filters.svg` into the page and add `class="pt-filters"` to `<html>`. Lithograph, printer and diagrams need the script.

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/install/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Inks and colours

*papertooth · Getting started*

Every ink, pencil, ribbon, highlighter, stamp pad and paper in Papertooth, in one place. The fountain pen inks are named after traditional Japanese colours (伝統色, dentō-shoku). Click any of them to use it across the site, then copy the settings.

## In your stylesheet

```
:root {
  --pt-pen: var(--pt-ink-ai);          /* fountain pen */
  --pt-brush: var(--pt-ink-sumi);      /* brush pen */
  --pt-marker: var(--pt-ink-sumi);     /* felt marker */
  --pt-ballpoint: var(--pt-bp-blue);
  --pt-graphite-c: var(--pt-pencil-hb);
  --pt-pencil: var(--pt-pencil-red);    /* coloured pencil */
  --pt-ribbon: var(--pt-ribbon-black);    /* typed text */
  --pt-hl: var(--pt-hl-yellow);            /* highlighter */
}

// pens, pencils and ribbons also recolour shapes already drawn, so set them from script too
kit.setPen('ink-ai'); kit.setPencil('pencil-red'); kit.setRibbon('ribbon-black');
```

The same list is exported as `PALETTE` from the script, if you need the names and values in JavaScript.

https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/colours/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Theming

*papertooth · Getting started*

Every effect is a CSS custom property. Set the grid, the paper and the fonts here and the whole site follows; copy the result into your own stylesheet. Inks and colours have their own page.

```html
:root {
  --pt-grid: 24px;
  --pt-dot-size: 0.8px;
  --pt-dot: rgba(88, 86, 80, 0.26);
  --pt-grain: 0.1;
  --pt-wobble: 1;
  --pt-font-type: "Courier Prime", monospace;
  --pt-font-hand: "Caveat", cursive;
}
```

Pens, pencils, ribbons and highlighters: see [Inks and colours](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/colours/).

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `--pt-grid` | 24px | Dot pitch and line height. Text snaps to it. |
| `--pt-sheet-width` | 720px | Widest the sheet gets, rounded down to whole cells. |
| `--pt-paper, --pt-desk` | #fefefe, #cdcbc5 | Paper and desk colours. |
| `--pt-dot, --pt-dot-size` | warm grey, .8px | Printed dots. |
| `--pt-line` | pale blue | Ruling on grid, graph and lined paper. |
| `--pt-grain` | .1 | Paper grain, 0 to 1. |
| `--pt-pen, --pt-pencil, --pt-ribbon` | indigo, red pencil, black | Current tools. |
| `--pt-hl` | yellow | Highlighter colour. |
| `--pt-wobble` | 1 | Letter wobble, 0 to 2. |
| `--pt-tilt` | 1 | Multiplies every --pt-rot, 0 to 2. |
| `--pt-draw, --pt-ease` | .75s | Drawing-on timing. |
| `--pt-font-type, -hand, -type-head, -jp` | Courier Prime, Caveat… | Fonts. |
| `--pt-s-body, -small, -h1, -h2` | 20, 16, 36, 26px | Type sizes. |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/theming/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Paper

*papertooth · Paper and writing*

Two separate choices: the paper itself (its colour and grain) and the ruling printed on it. The grid sets both the dot pitch and the line height, so text always sits on the ruling.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-paper` | white | white, cream, washi, kraft, recycled, tracing |
| `data-ruling` | dot | dot, grid, graph, lined, blank |
| `--pt-grid` | 24px | Dot pitch and line height |
| `--pt-grain` | .1 | Grain strength (each stock has its own) |
| `--pt-dot, --pt-line` | per paper | Ruling colours; each paper sets its own |
| `.pt-guides` |  | Show the baselines |
| `.pt-desk` |  | The desk colour, on body or any container. Dark at night, unless .pt-day. |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/paper/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT


---

# Writing

*papertooth · Paper and writing*

Typed or handwritten, in ribbon, pen or pencil. The texture varies the ink a little from letter to letter.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-wobble` |  | Each letter lands slightly differently, like a typewriter key |
| `.pt-mode-hand` |  | Handwriting instead of typing, on any ancestor |
| `.pt-pen-text, .pt-pencil-text, .pt-note` |  | Written with the fountain pen, a graphite pencil or the coloured pencil |
| `.pt-texture-light, .pt-texture-off` |  | Less or no ink texture |
| `--pt-wobble` | 1 | 0 to 2 |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/writing/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Highlighter

*papertooth · Marks*

A felt-tip swipe. Most styles start light where the nib lands and fill in towards the end; a flick and a dry marker start heavy and run out. On fresh ink the highlighter drags a little of the ink with it.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-hl` | swipe | swipe, flick, double, low, dry, scribble |
| `data-size` | regular | fine, broad |
| `data-color` | yellow | yellow, pink, green, orange, blue |
| `data-hover` | underline | underline (in pen), pass (a second highlighter pass), circle, none |
| `aria-pressed, aria-current, aria-expanded, aria-selected` |  | The button is on: its hover mark stays drawn (an open <details> too) |
| `:disabled, aria-disabled` |  | Faded, with no hover |
| `.pt-dry` |  | No fresh-ink smudge, on any ancestor |
| `--pt-hl` |  | Any colour |
| `kit.setFilters({ smudge })` | { drag: 4.2, blur: 3.4, strength: .78 } | How far and how strongly the ink drags |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/highlighter/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT


---

# Outlined button

*papertooth · Marks*

A drawn outline at rest, the highlighter on hover. Boxes, a loop, corners, or brackets of several kinds, including the Japanese 「」 and 【】.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-outline` | sketch | sketch, double, broken, circled, corners, brackets, parens, braces, angles, kagi, lenticular |
| `data-tool` | ink | pen, ballpoint, brush, marker, graphite, pencil |
| `data-color` | yellow | Hover highlighter colour |
| `data-hover` | pass | pass (highlighted), underline, circle, none |
| `aria-pressed, aria-current, aria-expanded, aria-selected` |  | The button is on: its hover mark stays drawn (an open <details> too) |
| `:disabled, aria-disabled` |  | Faded, with no hover |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/outline/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Link underline

*papertooth · Marks*

A pen stroke under each line of a link. Hover adds a second stroke, or circles the link.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-ul` | wobble | wobble, slant, double, swash, marker, wave, hl (highlighted; hover adds a pen underline) |
| `data-tool` | pen | ballpoint, brush, marker, graphite, pencil |
| `data-hover` | second | second (another stroke), circle, none |
| `aria-current` |  | The current page: its hover mark stays drawn (also aria-pressed, aria-expanded, aria-selected, an open <details>) |
| `aria-disabled` |  | Faded, with no hover |
| `--pt-visited` | the pen, a little darker | Colour of a visited link |
| `button.pt-link` |  | A button that reads as a link: none of the button’s own box |
| `.pt-links-mix` |  | On a container: a natural mix of styles |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/link/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Marks on text

*papertooth · Marks*

Circle, box, underline, strike or cross out a word. The teacher's hanamaru is for work well done.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-anno` |  | circle, box, under, strike, cross, hatch, hanamaru, x |
| `data-wrap` |  | Let a longer phrase wrap: strike, under and cross follow each line; circle, box and hanamaru go around the whole phrase |
| `data-tool` | coloured pencil | pen, ballpoint, brush, marker, graphite |
| `--pt-anno` |  | Any colour |

# Stamps

*papertooth · Marks*

Rubber stamps with real ink: heavier at the rim, uneven in the middle, with small gaps where the paper did not take it.

```html
<span class="pt-stamp pt-stamp--box">Approved</span>

// texture, for every stamp on the page
kit.setFilters({ stamp: { wear: 0.55, edge: 0.5, mottle: 0.5 } });
```

## Download the pictures

Each picture stamp is also a file of its own: one ink (it takes the colour around it, or black as an image) with real holes, so it sits on any paper. In a project they are `papertooth/stamps/frog.svg` and so on, and the stylesheet with all of them is optional (`papertooth/css/pictures`).

[ Tick](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/tick.svg)[ Star](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/star.svg)[ Heart](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/heart.svg)[ Arrow](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/arrow.svg)[ Cat 猫](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/cat.svg)[ Frog 蛙](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/frog.svg)[ Bear 熊](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/bear.svg)[ Tiger 虎](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/tiger.svg)[ Rabbit 兎](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/rabbit.svg)[ Tanuki 狸](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/tanuki.svg)[ Owl 梟](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/owl.svg)[ Cat paw 肉球](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/paw.svg)[ Onigiri](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/onigiri.svg)[ Sakura](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/sakura.svg)[ Smiling cloud](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/cloud.svg)[ Smiling sun](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/sun.svg)[ Daruma](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/daruma.svg)[ Mount Fuji](https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/stamps/fuji.svg)

## Approval boxes

The 承認 / 確認 / 作成 boxes found on Japanese office documents.

承認

確認

作成

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-stamp--box, .pt-stamp--round` |  | Text stamps. Any inline SVG drawn in currentColor works too |
| `data-pic` |  | A picture stamp, no script needed: tick, star, heart, arrow, cat, frog, bear, tiger, rabbit, tanuki, owl, paw, onigiri, sakura, cloud, sun, daruma, fuji. Give it role="img" and an aria-label; size with --pt-pic-size (60px) |
| `data-ink` | red | red, vermilion, blue, green, pink, brown |
| `--pt-rot` | 0deg | Rotation |
| `--pt-stamp-opacity` | .86 | How much ink |
| `kit.setFilters({ stamp })` | { wear: .55, edge: .5, mottle: .5, rough: 1.3 } | Texture |

# Date stamps

*papertooth · Marks*

The calendar stamps of Japanese stationery: a week strip to fill in, a month calendar, a year of months, or a single row. Fine printed lines in one ink, with today circled and the days gone by crossed out in pencil.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-unit` | week | week (a strip to fill in), month (a calendar), year (its months), day (1 to 31 in a row) |
| `data-variant` |  | bar: a single row for week, month or year; wide: a month as one long row of days |
| `data-rows` | 1 | Week strip and wide month: rows to fill in |
| `data-title` |  | Week strip: a title line on top (empty to write in, or printed text) |
| `data-date` | today | The day to mark, as 2026-10-21 |
| `data-mark` | circle | How today is marked: circle, box, highlight, none |
| `data-past` | none | How the past is marked: x, strike, none |
| `data-locale` | the page’s lang | Labels come from Intl in this language |
| `data-week-start` | the locale’s | 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday |
| `data-years, data-from` | 5, around today | Year bar |
| `data-mark-tool, data-past-tool` | pencil, graphite | The instruments the marks are drawn with |
| `data-ink` | red | red, vermilion, blue, green, pink, brown |
| `<DateStamp>` |  | The same in papertooth/react |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/datestamps/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Sticky notes

*papertooth · Paper goods*

Flat along the glue strip at the top. There is no outline: the edge you see is the shadow underneath. Four ways a note sits on a page, in the usual sizes.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-color` | yellow | yellow, pink, mint, blue, orange |
| `data-ratio` | square | wide, tall, small, strip |
| `data-sticky` | flat | lifted, pad, stack |
| `--pt-rot` | 0deg | Rotation |
| `--pt-note-paper` |  | Any paper colour |

# Tape

*papertooth · Paper goods*

Masking, kraft and washi tape are opaque, as they are in real life. Only clear tape lets the page through.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-tape` | masking | masking, kraft, stripes, dots, gingham, seigaiha, clear |
| `.pt-tape--text` |  | Tape you can write on |
| `--pt-rot` | 0deg | Rotation |

| `.pt-clip` |  | Paper clip, placed on the top edge |

# Lithograph

*papertooth · Images*

Any picture printed as a stone lithograph: grainy tones in one ink, two inks by tone, or three stones by colour like a chromolithograph, each slightly out of register.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-litho` | mono | mono, duo, tri |
| `--pt-litho-ink` | sumi | Mono and duo: main ink |
| `--pt-litho-ink2` | none | Duo: ink for the mid tones |
| `--pt-litho-blue, -red, -yellow` | blue, rose, yellow | Tri: one stone per colour |
| `--pt-litho-grain` | .6 | How much grain breaks the tones |
| `--pt-litho-size` | .7 | Grain frequency |
| `--pt-litho-contrast` | 1.2 |  |
| `--pt-litho-darken` | 0 | -0.3 to 0.3 |
| `--pt-litho-offset` | 1.5 | Misregistration, in px |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/litho/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Printer

*papertooth · Images*

The picture printed again at low resolution with real dithering, the way a Game Boy Printer or a thermal receipt printer would. The ink sits straight on the page.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-printer` | thermal | gameboy, thermal |
| `data-palette` | print | screen: the Game Boy's green |
| `data-dither` | printer default | bayer, atkinson, floyd, threshold |
| `data-dots` | 160 / 200 | Resolution across the picture |
| `--pt-print-contrast, -brightness` | 1.15, 0 |  |
| `--pt-print-wear` | .5 | Uneven heat |
| `--pt-print-ink` | #26262a | Ink colour |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/printer/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Frames

*papertooth · Images*

Ways to mount a picture: an instant print, photo corners, tape or a postage stamp. Any picture works, with or without an effect.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-photo[data-mount]` |  | polaroid, corners, or a .pt-tape inside |
| `--pt-photo-w` | 240px | Width |
| `--pt-photo-ratio` | 4 / 3 | Picture ratio (1 for the instant print) |
| `.pt-postage` |  | Perforated frame; wrap it in .pt-lift for a shadow |
| `--pt-perf` | 12px | Perforation pitch |
| `--pt-rot` | 0deg | Rotation |

# Day and week

*papertooth · Planner*

A date header and a week view, Monday first. Saturday is blue and Sunday red, as on Japanese calendars. With data-today they show today.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-dayhead[data-today]` |  | Filled with today by the script |
| `.pt-week[data-today]` |  | Dates for this week; today is circled |
| `kit.planner.dayHead(el, date)` |  | Any date |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/planner/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Habit tracker

*papertooth · Planner*

Tap a circle and it fills in with a quick scribble. Each habit has its own ink.

```html
<div class="pt-habits" style="--pt-days: 14">
  <div class="pt-habits__row" style="--pt-hb: var(--pt-ink-ai)">
    <span class="pt-habits__name">Write 500 words</span>
    <label class="pt-habit"><input type="checkbox" aria-label="Write 500 words, day 1"></label>
    <!-- one label per day -->
  </div>
</div>
```

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `--pt-days` | 14 | Columns |
| `--pt-hb` | pen | Ink for a row |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/habits/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Progress

*papertooth · Planner*

Pick the shape, then what it is filled with. A bar fills continuously; boxes and circles fill one at a time. 正 is how tallies are kept in Japan: five strokes to a character.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `data-shape` | bar | bar, boxes, circles, ring, tally, sei |
| `data-style` | highlight | The fill: highlight, pencil, hatch, cross, scribble, stipple |
| `--pt-value` | .5 | 0 to 1 (or aria-valuenow) |
| `data-tool` | ink | Any instrument |
| `data-segments` | 10 | How many boxes or circles |
| `data-max` | 20 | Tally total |
| `data-label` |  | Text shown beside it, or inside the ring |
| `--pt-hl` | yellow | Highlighter colour |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/progress/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Checkbox and radio

*papertooth · Forms*

Hand-drawn boxes and circles over the native controls, so keyboards and screen readers work as usual.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-check, .pt-radio` |  | Wrap a native input in a label |
| `data-tool` | pen | Instrument for the tick and the strike-through |
| `.pt-todo` |  | List of checkboxes on the grid |
| `data-strike` | line | line, double, scribble, under, none |
| `data-ul` | wobble | Underline style when data-strike="under" |

# Text field

*papertooth · Forms*

A line on the page to write on: dotted in pencil like a printed form, inked in when you start writing. What you type is written in pen.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `.pt-field` |  | Label and field together |
| `.pt-field__label` |  | Typed label above the line |
| `.pt-input` |  | Any text input, or a textarea for several ruled lines |
| `--pt-input-line` | pencil | Colour of the dotted line |

# Flowchart

*papertooth · Diagrams*

Write a Mermaid flowchart and it is drawn by hand. Colours and fonts follow the CSS variables, so a change of pen restyles it without drawing it again.

## Parameters

| Setting | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `Shapes` |  | A[rect] A(round) A([stadium]) A((circle)) A{diamond} A[[subroutine]] A[(cylinder)] A>flag] |
| `Edges` |  | --> --- -.-> ==> with |label| or -- label --> |
| `Direction` | TD | TD, LR, BT, RL |
| `data-fill` | none | wash, hatch, cross, scribble, stipple |
| `data-tool` | ink | pen, ballpoint, brush, marker, graphite, pencil, type |
| `--pt-diagram-stroke` | 1.6px | Line weight |

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/flowchart/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Script API

*papertooth · Reference*

Options for init(), and the methods on the returned kit.

```
const kit = Papertooth.init({
  root: document.body,   // where to look
  seed: null,            // a number makes every drawing repeatable
  filters: true,         // inject the texture filters
  filterParams: {        // tune any texture
    text: { density: .7 }, head: { rough: 1, density: .8 },
    graphite: { tooth: 2.4, rough: .9 },
    stamp: { wear: .55, rough: 1.3, edge: .5, mottle: .5 },
    smudge: { drag: 4.2, blur: 3.4, strength: .78 },
    smear: { drag: 7, blur: 4.5, strength: .7 },
    typewriter: { spread: .6, rough: 1.2, uneven: .7, speckle: .5 }
  },
  snap: true,            // put text on the grid
  lazy: true,            // draw shapes only near the screen
  motion: 'scroll',      // 'scroll', 'load' or 'none'
  stagger: .12,          // seconds between marks drawing on in one block
  highlight: 'swipe',    // default highlighter
  outline: 'sketch',     // default outline
  observe: true,         // enhance elements added later
  today: true,           // fill planner pieces marked data-today
  pen: null, pencil: null, ribbon: null, highlighter: null
});

kit.setPen('ink-beni');        // a token name or any colour
kit.setPencil('pencil-2b');
kit.setRibbon('ribbon-blue');
kit.setHighlighter('#ffc06a');
kit.setFilters({ stamp: { wear: .8 } });
kit.setTypewriter({ spread: .8 });
kit.refresh();                 // after changing writing mode or layout
kit.replay();                  // draw everything on again
kit.destroy();

Papertooth.renderDiagram(source, { font, seed, fill });   // SVG string
Papertooth.filtersMarkup(params);                         // the filters as SVG markup
```

## Performance

- Shapes are drawn only when they come near the screen, and redrawn only when their size or style changes.

- Each frame measures everything first and writes everything after, so the page lays out once.

- Snapping uses `translate`, which moves text without a new layout.

- The script ignores its own changes to the page and goes idle after loading.

- Animations are CSS only and stop for people who prefer reduced motion.

- Textures are SVG filters on text only. On long pages, use `.pt-texture-light`, or `.pt-lazy` on sections so the browser can skip them off screen.

---
https://tbudin.github.io/papertooth/api/ · papertooth 0.5.2 · MIT

# Changelog

*papertooth · Releases*

Newest first. [Follow by feed](../feed.xml).

## 0.5.2 - 2026-10-29 29 October 2026

### Fixed

- A node id with a hyphen broke a flowchart. `my-node --> other` was read as a node called `my`, and the edge after it was dropped without a word, leaving a stray node and no line. Ids keep their hyphens, and the Mermaid subset now has its own tests.

- A date stamp filled again in another language kept the `lang="ja"` it was given the first time, so a screen reader went on announcing the new text as Japanese.

- An annotation whose ink `<svg>` was written by hand with whitespace inside it threw while drawing, because the whitespace counted as one of its paths.

- A diagram or an image effect that finished loading after `destroy()` could still schedule a paint into a kit that was gone.

## 0.5.1 - 2026-10-29 29 October 2026

### Fixed

- Three-digit hex colours threw instead of resolving. `toRgb` read the colour with `Array#slice`, which a string does not have, so `#abc` failed wherever a colour is given as a short hex: `setPen`, `setPencil`, `setRibbon` and `setHighlighter`, the matching `init()` options (and the same keys in `data-pt-auto`), the ink filters, and the lithograph's ink. Six-digit hex, `rgb()` and the `pt-*` token names were never affected.

## 0.5.0 - 2026-10-24 24 October 2026

### Added

- Your own content in date stamp cells: a stamp picture, a letter, a mark, anything. Put an element inside the stamp with `data-day`, `data-date` or `data-month` (and `data-row` for a row to fill in); in React, return it from `cell({ part, row, date, state })`. It sits with the pencil marks, on top of the printed stamp, and stays when the stamp is filled again.

- Row labels: `data-rows="Run, Read, Water"` (or `rows={['Run', 'Read', 'Water']}`) writes them in a first column, on the wide month and the week strip.

- Every cell from `stampCells()` and `stampLayout()` carries the `date` it stands for, and cells in rows to fill in carry their `row`.

- A day heading and a week can show any day with `data-date="2026-10-21"` (until now only today, with `data-today`), and are written in `data-locale` or the page's `lang`.

- `data-week-label="Semaine {n}"` words a day heading's week number in any language (`weekLabel` in React also takes this string).

- `data-mark` on a week (`mark` on `<Week>`): today circled, boxed, highlighted or left plain.

- `cell({ habit, day, done })` on `<Habits>` draws a cell yourself, in place of its checkbox: a stamp, a letter, anything.

- The README shows how to use your own picture as a stamp (`--pt-pic`).

### Fixed

- A day heading always wrote "Week" in English, and the script filled day headings and weeks in British English whatever the page's language.

- A week's circle on today replaced the date's own `style` attribute, and filling the week again for another date left the old mark's settings behind. The circle's colour and offsets now come from the stylesheet.

## 0.4.1 - 2026-10-23 23 October 2026

### Changed

- The brush looks like brush ink: a heavier stroke with a ragged edge, dry streaks where the brush runs out, and uneven ink, on marks, checkboxes, diagrams, and drawn underlines and rules. Before, it was a thick, even line, close to the fountain pen and the marker. Tune it with `setFilters({ brush: { dry, rough } })`.

- A date stamp tells screen readers what it marks: a month calendar says the day it marks (Wednesday 21 October 2026), a year of months says the month. Before, a month calendar only said the month. `stampLabel()` takes `{ mark, variant }` for this.

### Fixed

- Buttons swung between two grid positions each time the page was snapped again (when an app changed the page, for example). The press effect animated `translate`, which snapping reads, so a snap measured the button mid-animation; the press now uses `transform`.

## 0.4.0 - 2026-10-23 23 October 2026

### Added

- Picture stamps in the stylesheet, no script needed: `<span class="pt-stamp" data-pic="frog">`. Six new animals (frog, bear, tiger, rabbit, tanuki, owl) join tick, star, heart, arrow, cat, paw, daruma, Fuji, sakura, onigiri, cloud and sun.

- Date stamps, `.pt-datestamp` and `<DateStamp>`, in the manner of Japanese stationery stamps: a week strip to fill in (with rows and a title line), a month calendar with the 1st on its weekday and a month selector, a year of months, and single-row bars. Fine printed lines in one ink, labels in any language through Intl; today circled, boxed or highlighted, the days gone by crossed out or struck through in pencil.

- Per-part stylesheets: `papertooth/css/base` and then only the parts a page uses (`highlight`, `marks`, `pictures`, `planner`…), in any order. `papertooth/css` is still everything.

- Picture stamps as files of their own: `papertooth/stamps/frog.svg` and so on (one ink, real holes), also downloadable from the docs site.

- `papertooth/diagram` for `renderDiagram` and `kindOf`.

- A wide month stamp, `data-variant="wide"` (`variant="wide"`): the whole month in one row, each day under its weekday, with rows to fill in like a habit tracker.

- Every state of a button and a link: - pressed down (`:active`), and on (`aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current` or an open `<details>`), which keeps the hover mark drawn; - disabled (`disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"`); - visited links (`--pt-visited`); - reduced motion, and a plain underline and border in high-contrast mode; - `button.pt-link` and `summary` as buttons or links.

- An `x` mark on text (`data-anno="x"`).

- `data-wrap` on a mark (`wrap` on `<Anno>`) lets a longer phrase wrap: a strike, underline or scribble follows each line, a circle, box or hanamaru goes around the whole phrase.

- React planner components: `<DayHead>`, `<Week>` (with `children` to fill each day), `<Habit>` and `<Habits>`. They render everything themselves, so nothing is written into React's DOM afterwards.

- Date helpers with no DOM, in any locale and from any first day of the week: `weekDates`, `firstDayOf`, `dayParts`, `sameDay`, `stampCells`, `stampLabel` (and `isoWeek`, as before). `dayHead()` and `week()` take `{ locale }` and `{ locale, weekStart }`.

- `papertooth/shapes` and `papertooth/tokens`: the shape generators, picture stamps and colours with no DOM, for React Native, canvas or a server.

- `papertooth/layer.css`: the stylesheet inside `@layer papertooth`, so utility classes (Tailwind v4) can win over it.

- Browser tests (Playwright) and CI. Releases are published from a version tag by a GitHub workflow with npm trusted publishing, and copied to GitHub Packages as `@tbudin/papertooth`.

### Changed

- As a module, the script fetches the code for diagrams and image effects only when a page has one: about 23 KB gzipped up front instead of 30. The `<script>` build is still one file with everything.

- `renderDiagram` moved from `papertooth` to `papertooth/diagram` (it stays on `window.Papertooth` in the `<script>` build).

- White paper is a neutral white (`#fefefe`) with a grey grain at `.1`, so it reads white on a whole screen; cream and kraft keep the warm grain (`--pt-grain-warm-image`).

- To-do lists, bullet journals and anything marked `data-pt-ruled` snap to the grid as one block, so rows an app sizes and rules itself keep their rhythm.

- The sheet's text styles, headings included, weigh as little as one class (through `:where()`), so an app's own class wins over them when it loads later. Within papertooth, the per-part stylesheets can load in any order.

- `.pt-sheet--page` is an ordinary block instead of a column with a grid line of gap between everything on it. Its blocks of text keep that line between them, but an app's header, tabs and views no longer get it added on top of their own spacing.

- A `<section>` on a sheet is no longer a flex column. It puts a grid line between its blocks of text with margins, which an app can override and which merge with the app's own margins instead of adding to them. Before, every section in an app became a flex column, which shrank centred children with a `max-width` and stacked its gap on the app's margins.

- Hovering a highlighter button underlines it in pen instead of adding a second highlighter pass, which is now `data-hover="pass"`. Outlined buttons still bring out the highlighter.

- Hover marks on buttons and links are drawn only where a pointer can hover, so a tap on a phone no longer leaves one stuck; a tap draws it while the finger is down.

- A highlighted link (`data-ul="hl"`) is highlighted from the start, and hovering draws a pen underline under it instead of more highlighter.

- The weekend in `.pt-week` is coloured by `data-day` (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday), so it is right wherever the week starts. Markup without `data-day` is still read as Monday first.

### Fixed

- On `.pt-sheet--page`, a `--pt-sheet-pad` smaller than a grid cell rounded the side margins to nothing on phones; they are now at least one cell.

- A to-do that wraps onto several lines is struck through line by line and takes as many grid lines as it needs, instead of overflowing into the next one. The strike now sits on an inline `.pt-check__ink` inside `.pt-check__text` (the script and `<Check>` add it).

- A sticky note in a flex row or grid that stretches its items kept its shadows at the bottom of the stretched box, below the paper.

## 0.3.1 - 2026-10-23 23 October 2026

### Added

- `drawInserted` option: `false` shows content added on screen (a route or tab change) as already drawn. `kit.settle(element)` does the same for one part of the page.

### Changed

- The script keeps its state in `data-pt-*` attributes instead of classes (`is-drawn`, `is-painted`, `is-ready`, `pt-selecting`, `pt-motion` and others), so a framework changing `className` no longer undoes it. `class="pt-filters"` still works for pages that paste the filters themselves.

- A picture the printer cannot read gets `data-pt-blocked` instead of the `pt-print--blocked` class.

### Fixed

- `init()` after `destroy()` (a remount, React StrictMode) left blocks below the fold invisible.

- `<Wobble>` did not split `Hello {name}`; screen readers now get the whole text and the letters are hidden from them.

- `<Btn>` rendered its children twice (duplicate ids, duplicated state); the smear is now text only.

- React components forward refs on React 18 (`<Check>` to its input).

## 0.3.0 - 2026-10-23 23 October 2026

### Added

- `papertooth/react`: `<Btn>`, `<Mark>`, `<Anno>`, `<Wobble>` and `<Check>` render the markup the script would add, so React re-renders keep it; `usePapertooth()` and `<Papertooth />` start and stop the script. Marked `"use client"` for Next.js.

- TypeScript types for the script and the React components.

- A React and Next.js section in the README.

### Changed

- CDN snippets point at `@0.3`.

## 0.2.2 - 2026-10-22 23 October 2026

### Added

- Night inks: on the dark desk, links, highlights, ticks, rules, stamps and tape written straight on the desk switch to light inks (`--pt-night-pen`, `--pt-night-pencil`, `--pt-night-graphite`, `--pt-night-ballpoint`, `--pt-night-hl-ink`); paper keeps its day inks.

- Text on the desk takes `--pt-desk-ink`.

- The script redraws when the system switches between light and dark.

### Fixed

- Buttons no longer stretch in grid or column layouts, so their highlight fits the label.

- The draw-on wipe releases its clip when it ends, so nothing drawn past an element's box stays cut off.

- Checkbox outlines, bullet-journal signs and the progress label follow the text colour.

## 0.2.1 - 2026-10-22 23 October 2026

### Fixed

- A progress bar's label was cut off after it drew on.

- The highlight on a chosen colour swatch ran past its name.

## 0.2.0 - 2026-10-22 23 October 2026

First public release.
